lines.say: What if this young queen
has to find her own death completely blind?
This is The Execution of Lady Jane Grey,
painted by Paul Delaroche in 1833.
Jane kneels in white on the straw,
an old lieutenant at her side
and the executioner waiting.
But look at her hand.
Her fingers reach for the block.
Jane can't see the block.
Jane can't touch it. Jane just keeps searching.
According to the National Gallery,
she was seventeen
and had been queen for only nine days.
A crowned girl should never kneel like this.
But Queen Mary had her beheaded anyway.
And here's the unsettling part.
Every eye in the room sees the block,
yet Jane must search.
Almost as if she
is made to choose it herself.
So what is that hand really reaching for?
